quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #4
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: Before starting the engine, you should:

options.text: Make sure only backseat passengers have fastened their seat belts.
Make sure only adult passengers have fastened their seat belts.
Make sure only child passengers have fastened their seat belts.
Make sure all passengers have fastened their seat belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure all passengers have fastened their seat belts.
questions.explanation: Get in the habit of fastening your seat belt before you start driving. Make sure all passengers do the same.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Steep hill ahead.
Pedestrian crossing ahead.
Low railroad crossing.
Low clearance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low clearance.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the bridge or overpass ahead has limited height. Do not proceed if your vehicle is taller than the height shown on the sign (in this case, 13 feet 6 inches).

questions.question: The best way to reduce your risk of injury or death in a crash is to:

options.text: Wear your seat belt.
Drive only on weekdays.
Stay in the right lane on highways with multiple lanes.
Drive only between 3:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear your seat belt.
questions.explanation: Wearing your seat belt is the single most effective thing you can do to protect yourself from death or injury while driving.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing red or blue lights?

options.text: Try to reach your destination before it catches up to you.
Keep driving but try to stay out of its way.
Pull to the side of the road and stop completely.
Stop in the middle of an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and stop completely.
questions.explanation: You must give the right-of-way to all emergency vehicles using sirens, air horns, or flashing red, blue, or white lights. Pull to the right edge of the road when possible. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first before pulling over.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts to cross in front of your car. You should:

options.text: Flash your lights.
Slow down.
Speed up and drive in front of the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian cross.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be ready to stop when you see pedestrians on or crossing the road. Be extra careful where children are present. Always let pedestrians cross in crosswalks.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No right turn.
Keep right.
No U-turn.
Left lane must turn left.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This regulation sign tells drivers what they must or must not do. This sign means you cannot turn right at this location.

questions.question: Seat belts:

options.text: Should be worn at all times when driving or riding in a vehicle.
Should be worn only when driving at high speeds.
Should be worn loosely.
Can only protect the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be worn at all times when driving or riding in a vehicle.
questions.explanation: Seat belts save lives. They must be worn every time you drive or ride in a vehicle. They are the most important safety feature in any car.

questions.question: When towing a heavy trailer that weighs more than half the towing vehicle's weight, or weighs 3,000 pounds or more, the trailer must have:

options.text: Brakes.
Breakaway protection.
Hub caps.
Brakes and breakaway protection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brakes and breakaway protection.
questions.explanation: If your trailer weighs more than half the towing vehicle's weight or weighs 3,000 pounds or more, it must have both brakes and breakaway protection.

questions.question: A sign of a drunk driver is:

options.text: They are weaving between lanes.
They are driving slower than other traffic.
They are making quick and sudden stops.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Signs of drunk driving include speeding, weaving between lanes, driving slower than traffic, making jerking movements, and making sudden stops.

questions.question: Don't follow other cars too closely because:

options.text: You may not see the road between the cars.
You may not have time to stop if the car in front suddenly slows or stops.
You may not see the car's turn signals.
You may not see the car's brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not have time to stop if the car in front suddenly slows or stops.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely, you may not have enough time to stop if the car in front suddenly slows or stops, which could cause a collision.

questions.question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, what must you do?

options.text: Slow down until it passes.
Drive with your flashers on.
Pull to the side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear an emergency vehicle siren, you must pull to the side of the road and stop.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You are about to enter a one-way street going the wrong way.
U-turns are not allowed.
You may go if the road is clear.
You must stop completely before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are about to enter a one-way street going the wrong way.
questions.explanation: If you drive past this sign, you are going the wrong way. You could crash head-on with other cars. Turn around carefully.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection or into a driveway, you must:

options.text: Leave room on your right for other vehicles to pass.
Let vehicles coming toward you go first.
Not cross any solid yellow line.
Not block vehicles coming from behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let vehicles coming toward you go first.
questions.explanation: When turning left, let all oncoming traffic pass that could be a danger to you. Only turn when the opposite lane is clear and safe.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on a highway, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in your car and wait for help.
Turn on your hazard flashers to warn other drivers.
Honk your horn at passing cars.
Flash your headlights at oncoming cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your hazard flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: When your car breaks down on the highway, turn on your hazard flashers. Move as far off the road as possible. Lift your hood so other drivers know your car is broken.

questions.question: What should you do to change lanes?

options.text: Check mirrors and signal, then change lanes.
Signal, check mirrors, check your blind spot over your shoulder, then change lanes.
Signal, check mirrors, and change lanes.
Signal and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, check your blind spot over your shoulder, then change lanes.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, turn on your signal. Check your rearview and side mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Make sure no other car is in the lane you want to enter. Only change lanes when it is safe.

questions.question: What can make it harder to drive safely?

options.text: Alcohol.
Any medication.
Not getting enough sleep.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Safe driving requires you to be in good physical condition. Alcohol, drugs, and being tired can all make it harder to drive safely.

questions.question: On major highways, you should:

options.text: Stay alert.
Keep your eyes moving.
Be ready to react to dangers.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stay alert on highways and be ready for unexpected dangers. Do not look at any one thing for more than a few seconds. This prevents highway hypnosis.

questions.question: When you see railroad tracks ahead, what should you do?

options.text: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
Speed up to cross before the gate lowers.
Drive around a lowered gate.
Do not worry about how many tracks there are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When you approach railroad tracks, look and listen for trains. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: Which statement about speed is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
Speeding can kill.
Speeding is safe if you are a good driver.
Both "Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous" and "Speeding can kill."

questions.correctAnswerText: Both "Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous" and "Speeding can kill."
questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the more likely a crash will cause death. At speeds above 80 miles per hour, survival is almost impossible. Driving much slower than other traffic is also dangerous because other drivers may make risky moves to pass you.

questions.question: When you see a school bus stopped with its stop arm out, you must:

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait.
Honk your horn before passing on the left.
Keep driving when you think all kids have exited.
Pass the bus before its door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has its stop arm out, you must stop completely. Do not move until the stop arm goes up.

questions.question: Anything that requires you to ____ could cause you to crash.

options.text: Take your eyes off the road
Take your hands off the wheel
Take your attention away from driving
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that takes your attention off driving, your eyes off the road, or your hands off the wheel.

questions.question: If a sign does not prohibit it, a driver stopped at a red light may:

options.text: Turn right after yielding to other traffic and pedestrians.
Never turn right.
Turn right at any time.
Turn right only after honking the horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn right after yielding to other traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: You may turn right at a red light unless a sign says you cannot. You must let all pedestrians and vehicles pass first.

questions.question: Alcohol causes:

options.text: Loss of concentration.
Poor coordination.
Slower judgment.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol harms your vision, judgment, concentration, and coordination.

questions.question: You must signal before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb:

options.text: Only if other traffic is near.
Always, and it is required by law.
Only during the move, not before.
Not necessary if you move slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always, and it is required by law.
questions.explanation: Signal at least 100 feet before you turn or change lanes. Always signal before pulling away from a curb so other drivers know your plans.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No U-turn.
Two-way left turn.
Minimum speed limit.
No parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This regulation sign tells drivers they cannot make U-turns where this sign is posted.

questions.question: Highway markings:

options.text: Are usually not important.
Are only found in construction zones.
Help guide drivers on the road.
Are usually red and blue.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help guide drivers on the road.
questions.explanation: Road markings help you stay in the correct lane, show safe passing zones, and warn you about changes ahead.

questions.question: You have a green light, but pedestrians are crossing against the red. You should:

options.text: Honk your horn.
Speed up and drive in front of them.
Stop and let them cross safely.
Drive close to scare them into following the rules.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let them cross safely.
questions.explanation: Always let pedestrians cross safely, even if you have a green light. Be careful around all pedestrians.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Check your side mirror.
Check your rearview mirror.
Turn your head to check for vehicles in your blind spot.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Check both mirrors and look over your shoulder before changing lanes. This helps you see all traffic around you, including vehicles in your blind spot.

questions.question: Stress can affect your driving by:

options.text: Making it harder to focus on the road.
Decreasing your chances of an accident.
Making you fall asleep at the wheel.
Making you more aware of others.

questions.correctAnswerText: Making it harder to focus on the road.
questions.explanation: Emotions like worry, anger, fear, or sadness reduce your ability to focus on driving. If you feel emotionally upset, wait to drive until you are calm.

questions.question: The best safety protection in a crash is:

options.text: Only a lap and shoulder belt.
Only an airbag.
A lap/shoulder belt and an airbag together.
No safety restraints.

questions.correctAnswerText: A lap/shoulder belt and an airbag together.
questions.explanation: Seat belts double your chances of surviving a crash and greatly reduce serious injury. Airbags work best with seat belts for added protection in front-end crashes. Always wear both.
